investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted), and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window (~143–147 s), the agent VM was never created, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots on the only affinity-matching nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 qualify for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource), making the cluster effectively smaller than its total node count for remote-agent workloads. A recent change to node labels or pod affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node pool.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have insufficient total VM slot capacity for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

QUATERNARY — Peer-pod provider or VM quota limit at the infrastructure layer (e.g., cloud provider VM quota beneath the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource): the extended resource count reported to the scheduler may be capped by an external quota, not just node count.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted), and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval timeout window (~143–147 s), the agent VM was never created, and no required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity/scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots on the only affinity-matching nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for a new agent pod. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's node affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 qualify for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource), making the cluster effectively smaller than its total node count for remote-agent workloads. A recent change to node labels or pod affinity rules could have reduced the eligible node pool.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning for peak load: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have insufficient total VM slot capacity for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

QUATERNARY — Peer-pod provider or VM quota limit at the infrastructure layer (e.g., cloud provider VM quota beneath the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource): the extended resource count reported to the scheduler may be capped by an external quota, not just node count.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-29 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector requirements. When the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918) called createAgent with type "remote", the resulting pod was placed in the Unschedulable state for 147 seconds before the eval timed out. No agent was ever created, so no runtime response was produced and no evidence was collected. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents eval checks in production-api and is not evidence of a broader service outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes and no preemption victims were found, indicating all VM slots are occupied by existing workloads.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements, meaning even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were freed on those nodes it would not help without affinity changes.

[Medium confidence] Cluster has not scaled out to add additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes: the fixed pool of 6 nodes with only 2 eligible suggests no autoscaling event occurred during the ~150s scheduling window.

[Low confidence] A concurrent workload spike consumed all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots just before the eval run, causing transient exhaustion that may self-resolve; no historical run data is available to confirm or deny recurrence (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).
